sara: quick heads-up — ran token-capacity slicing experiments in prod-shadow this morning. noticed p95 regressions when FlashAttention and paged-KV are both active for mixed-length workloads. digging notes below.

devin: can you paste the numbers? p95/p99? :eyes:

sara: profile snapshot (aggregated): p50=55ms, p95=230ms, p99=420ms.
- kernel-switch spikes line up with sequences crossing ~1.1k-1.4k tokens.
- paged-KV page faults / prefetch latency ~= 10-15ms per page on these traces.
- memcpy stalls (CPU->GPU) visible in nvprof around the same timestamps.

kyle: interesting — so it's not raw compute, it's the combo of kernel hysteresis + KV prefetch causing tail. did you capture any flamegraphs?

sara: small flame: kernel_select hot path shows repeated select()->compile fallback on ~600 concurrent batches when sequence distribution is bimodal. repeated toggles cause batching to wait for the right kernel which increases queue time.

sam: oof. sounds like our continuous-batcher is too eager to wait for ideal kernel. any config changes tried?

sara: tried two quick experiments:
1) slot-based batching with a token-capacity slicing heuristic (pack by token budget rather than request count). token_budget_target=2048, slot_size_tokens=256, max_wait_ms=12. result: p95 dropped to ~170ms, p99 to ~320ms. kernel switch count down ~48%.
2) hysteresis window: add kernel_hysteresis_ms=8 so we avoid flipping kernels for short-lived bursts. further reduced oscillation but increased average CPU by ~3%.

alisa: can you share the batcher config snippet? would like to run on dedicated canary cluster.

sara: paste config we used:
```
queue:
  mode: slot
  slot_size_tokens: 256
  max_wait_ms: 12
  token_budget_target: 2048
  kernel_hysteresis_ms: 8
  fallback_kernel: "vectorized-matmul"
  paged_kv_prefetch_pages: 2
```

devin: fallback_kernel is key. FlashAttention yields best throughput, but when paged-KV causes page thrash the vectorized-matmul fallback keeps latency predictable. what about adaptive prefetch?

sara: tested paged_kv_prefetch_pages=4 briefly; lowered page faults but increased GPU memory pressure and memcpy time. sweet spot seems 2 pages for our cluster type.

kyle: any change to admission policy? i.e., prefer short sequences to avoid blocking long seqs that cause kernel swap?

sara: added short-first admission in slot-packer: if a slot has >60% short-seq (<256) then dispatch early unless token_budget_target already exceeded. that helps tail for short requests without unduly delaying long ones.

ci-bot: perf-check: canary run 2026-03-15T09:12Z — p95 improvement 26%, p99 improvement 18%, CPU cost +3.1%, overall tokens/sec -1.2%. link: https://ci.redwood/profiles/1748889999

sam: nice. action items?

sara: short list:
- run canary on dedicated cluster for 24h with these settings (slot batching + kernel_hysteresis + paged_kv_prefetch_pages=2). assign @kyle.
- instrument kernel_select to emit a lightweight metric every flip (avoid full tracing) — assign @devin.
- try lowering kernel_hysteresis_ms to 4 for a follow-up test to see tradeoff. assign @alisa.

kyle: I'll schedule the canary today and add dashboards for flip_rate and slot_fill_ratio.

devin: will add the flip_count metric and a tiny prometheus exporter. should be non-invasive.

alisa: will run a secondary test with hysteresis=4 and report delta.

sam: thanks all — great quick iteration. moving to tracking issue #INF-981 to capture follow-ups. :thumbsup:

sara: thanks — will post results here once canary finishes. :rocket:
